claim: Across the Polonnaruwa period the monetary system shifted away from the earlier gold Kahavanu/Massa tradition toward increasingly base-metal and copper issues; by the late twelfth and early thirteenth centuries copper Massa issues were common, silver could be used only as a wash on base metal, and Dharmasokadeva's 1208 issue was copper.
bounded_by: This establishes a change in monetary metal and quality, not inflation rates, money supply, purchasing power, fiscal insolvency or a direct causal path to the fall of Polonnaruwa.
notes: The museum photograph is useful as a field anchor; the historical proposition is independently anchored in institutional and specialist numismatic sources.
